Selective inference

infer_selective.Rd

Inference that conditions on the selection event, via the selectiveInference package: selectiveInference::fixedLassoInf() for lasso select_glmnet() selectors (alpha = 1), and selectiveInference::fsInf() for forward select_stepwise_ic() selectors (gaussian family only).

Usage

infer_selective(
  object,
  data,
  nonselection = c("ignored", "confident_nulls", "uncertain_nulls"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  use_cv_sigma = FALSE,
  sigma = NULL,
  on_mismatch = c("warn-fall-back", "silent-fall-back", "stop"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a selector object

data

the data used to fit the selector

nonselection

how to handle variables the selector did not select; one of "ignored", "confident_nulls" or "uncertain_nulls". See infer_upsi() for what each does; here, too, "uncertain_nulls" intervals are not adjusted for selection.

conf.level

.95 by default

use_cv_sigma

estimate Sigma via CV (if FALSE, uses SI defaults)

sigma

optional known or pre-computed residual standard deviation. When supplied it is passed straight through to the selectiveInference function and no sigma is estimated. The automatic estimate used when p > n/2 calls selectiveInference::estimateSigma() (for glmnet), which runs cross-validation, thus important to set.seed().

on_mismatch

what to report when the selector's stopping point and selectiveInference's disagree. For stepwise_ic selectors the two minimize slightly different criteria and can disagree. Inference falls back to the model the selector returned, by conditioning on a fixed number of steps; this argument controls how loudly that is reported:

  • "warn-fall-back" (default) warns and points at select_stepwise_ic(criterion = "cp"), which makes the two rules agree.

  • "silent-fall-back" falls back quietly.

  • "stop" errors instead.

The fallback does not account for uncertainty in how many variables were selected, proceeding as though the number of steps had been pre-ordained; the effect of this appears to be minor.

For glmnet selectors, inference always conditions on a refit of the lasso at the selected lambda with a tight convergence tolerance (thresh = 1e-14), since glmnet's default tolerance can leave the active set or signs slightly off on correlated designs, which makes intervals undercover. If the refit's active set or signs differ from the selector's, the same three options control whether this is reported with a warning, silently, or as an error.

...

arguments passed to selectiveInference function(s)

Value

an inferrer object; see tidy.inferrer()
